messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased 5xx from service 'web-api' in us-west-2 (usw2) observed by synthetic checks (latency spike + error rate). Root cause suspected in ELB/target connectivity. Pager: @tia oncall.

tia: Seeing spikes in Grafana, ELB 5xxCount trending up across several target groups in us-west-2a/2b. App servers show TCP resets to ELB. Repro: curl -i https://api.redwood-inference.com/health returns 502 intermittently.

rafa: Confirmed. CloudWatch: ELB TargetHealth shows "initial"/"unhealthy" flapping for targets in us-west-2a. I'm seeing increased Latency and SurgeQueueFull metric on NLB/ALB.

mike: Are EBS volumes impacted? Any IO errors on EC2? I checked Node exporter metrics — disk IO looks normal. Kernel logs show network interface errors on a subset of instances:

```
Mar 15 12:05:23 ip-10-0-1-23 kernel: igb 0000:02:00.0 eth0: Tx timeout
Mar 15 12:06:11 ip-10-0-1-23 kernel: eth0: link down
```

ops-lead: Seems like an AZ network fabric degradation affecting instance NICs. Route53 healthchecks are still reporting healthy because they hit other AZs; however, DNS failover is not triggering fast due to TTL and healthcheck propagation.

tia: Customer impact: ~15% requests to hosted API from customers hitting us-west-2 are 5xx. Global traffic auto-routed to other regions for most customers but some hardcoded endpoints still point to us-west-2 bucket. Support queue is getting latency tickets.

eliza: I'm on support, triaging inbound tickets. I'll send customers the interim status note once we have mitigation steps.

rafa: Live mitigation proposal:
- Move traffic away from affected AZ (us-west-2a) by marking targets unhealthy at ELB level and enabling cross-zone balancing.
- Lower Route53 TTL for api domain for faster failover (currently 300s -> 30s) and create a weighted record to shift weight to us-west-2b/c or us-east-1 as fallback.
- Increase connection draining on ALB to 300s to avoid abrupt drops while draining.

mike: Steps to mark targets unhealthy (run on aws CLI):

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn <arn> --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=300
aws elbv2 set-rule-priorities -- ... (we'll script per targetgroup)
```

tia: I'll perform ELB target adjustments for web-api-targetgroup-1 and -2. Rafa, help me coordinate Route53 changes.

rafa: I'll provision a temporary weighted record and lower TTL. Plan:
1) Create new weighted record api-weighted.usw2 (60% us-west-2b/c, 40% us-east-1)
2) Set original api A/ALIAS TTL -> 30
3) Monitor error rate for 10m then cutover heavier weight to fallback if errors persist

support-bot: Automated: Created incident in Zendesk with high priority, linked to this thread. Incident ID: ZD-48217.

eliza: Noting customer impact and initial outbound message draft: "We're investigating increased errors in us-west-2; traffic mitigation underway; no data loss; next update in 15m." Will post after ops-lead approves.

ops-lead: Approve message. Also notify SRE oncall in us-east for capacity headroom in case we shift traffic.

tia: Executing target deregistration: marking 8 hosts in targetgroup-1 unhealthy in us-west-2a. Applying cross-zone load balancing toggle.

rafa: Route53 change applied: TTL 300 -> 30 for api.example.com (Route53 console change ID: r53chg-98765). Created weighted RR set with weights pointing to us-west-2b/c and us-east-1.

mike: Checking downstream services — cache clusters in us-west-2 still reachable. Need to ensure session affinity fallback works when traffic moves.

tia: Rolling out changes complete. Early telemetry: 5xx rate dropped from 15% -> 3% over last 5m. Latency for failing requests decreased.

incident-bot: Timeline event: ELB target deregistration + Route53 TTL change detected at 2026-03-15T12:22:10Z by automation.

eliza: Posted customer status update to support portal. Link: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/zd-48217

support-bot: Noted 12 open tickets referencing "us-west" or "502". Escalating to enterprise support for customers with SLAs.

ops-lead: Preliminary impact assessment: Regional partial degradation localized to us-west-2a; cross-AZ failover reduced customer visible errors. No data loss. Estimated root cause: network fabric issues in us-west-2a causing NIC flaps and ELB target health instability. Next steps: continue monitoring, keep TTL low for 1 hour, plan instance replacements in the affected AZ, and involve AWS support.

rafa: I've opened an AWS support case (case# 1234567890) and provided packet captures and instance logs. Requesting AWS to check their AZ switchplane and any fabric maintenance.

tia: On-call handoff plan: I'll stay for the next 40m then hand to @rafa for monitoring and postmortem. Handoff note: mitigations applied, Route53 TTL lowered, targets deregistered, 5xx down to ~3%, SLAs for enterprise customers being monitored.

mike: I can start preparing replacement AMIs and a rolling replace plan for instances in the affected ASG in us-west-2a. Will coordinate with infra to avoid simultaneous AZ impact.

eliza: Will send follow-up customer note in 30m with status and ETA for full resolution.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: RESOLUTION: AWS acknowledged networking issue in us-west-2a and marked related fabric incident as UNDER INVESTIGATION. Our mitigations sustained reduced customer impact. Incident severity de-escalated at 2026-03-15T13:50:11Z.

ops-lead: Postmortem owners: @rafa (lead), @tia (mitigations), @mike (infra remediation), @eliza (customer comms). Deadline: initial postmortem draft in 72 hours.

tia: Handing off to @rafa now. Leaving notes in the incident doc and linking packet captures.

rafa: Taking over. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and start the postmortem doc.

eliza: Closing the immediate support queue items and flagging enterprise customers for follow-up.

support-bot: Auto: Incident ZD-48217 updated: status -> monitoring. Notifying subscribed customers.

mike: Adding runbook updates: add a checklist for lowering TTL and creating weighted failover in Route53 for regional ELB anomalies.

ops-lead: Good work team. We'll compile timeline and root cause once AWS provides a full RCA. Thank you everyone.
